claims.text: Cipher Digital reports 907 MW of operating and contracted capacity across three hyperscale campuses in Texas.
The extension lifts contracted revenue at Barber Lake from $3.8B to more than $9B.
Cipher sold $810M of 6.0% notes to fund Stingray through completion.
Bitcoin mining brought in $24.8M of revenue in Q2 2026, and the company posted a net loss of $267.5M as interest expense rose to $66.7M.
Its portfolio covers 5.3 GW across 11 sites in Texas and Ohio, and 83% of that capacity has no tenant yet.
In June 2026 it announced plans for a 500 MW campus next to a Texas power plant, and in August it took an option on a site near San Antonio, called Apollo, for up to 900 MW.
Under the Barber Lake extension Cipher pays the first $359.3M of cost overruns and the tenant repays half of any further overruns as extra rent.
Cipher carried $5.45B of long-term borrowings and $831.8M of cash at the end of June 2026, so new campuses depend on project bond markets.
Signing tenants for the pipeline sites, including Apollo, is the next test.
Barber Lake lease = 20 years, more than $9B (September 2026)
Operating and contracted capacity = 907 MW
Portfolio = 5.3 GW across 11 sites
Q2 2026 = Revenue $24.8M, net loss $267.5M

claims.text: QumulusAI traces back to two 2019 companies, WAHA Technologies and WAHA, Inc., which merged in December 2022 as Global Digital Holdings.
In April 2025 the company acquired The Cloud Minders, a GPU-as-a-Service business it had first invested in in October 2023, and rebranded as QumulusAI.
It adopted the name legally in August 2025 and still lists blockchain hosting facilities in Watonga, Oklahoma and Denton, Texas.
Q2 2026 revenue was $6.7M, up 118% from a year earlier, with AI compute at 84% of the total.
The deployed fleet reached 3,088 GPUs, and cumulative signed contract value stood at $282.5M in August 2026.
It deploys capacity in colocation sites in metro Atlanta, Kansas City, Denver and Philadelphia and sizes each build to signed demand.
The company guides to $300M of forward annual recurring revenue and 18 MW of capacity by the end of fiscal 2026.
It also cites a line of sight to 2.5 GW by the end of fiscal 2027, against 8 MW under executed agreements in August 2026.
Q2 2026 revenue = $6.7M, up 118%
Deployed GPUs = 3,088, Q2 2026
